passages.text: Then the word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time: “Get up! Go to the great city of Nineveh and proclaim to it the message that I give you.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jonah a second time.
Jonah was a prophet.
The LORD said, “Get up.
Go to Nineveh.
Nineveh is a great city.
Proclaim to Nineveh the message I give you.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֧י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־ יוֹנָ֖ה שֵׁנִ֥ית לֵאמֹֽר׃ ק֛וּם לֵ֥ךְ אֶל־ נִֽינְוֵ֖ה הָעִ֣יר הַגְּדוֹלָ֑ה וִּקְרָ֤א אֵלֶ֙יהָ֙ אֶת־ הַקְּרִיאָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י דֹּבֵ֥ר אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: This time Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, in accordance with the word of the LORD. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, requiring a three-day journey.
passages.sermon:
Jonah was a prophet.
The LORD spoke to Jonah.
Jonah obeyed the LORD.
Jonah got up.
Jonah went to Nineveh.
Jonah did what the LORD commanded.
Nineveh was a very large city.
Nineveh was important to God.
It took three days to walk through Nineveh.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣קָם יוֹנָ֗ה וַיֵּ֛לֶךְ אֶל־ נִֽינְוֶ֖ה כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה וְנִֽינְוֵ֗ה הָיְתָ֤ה עִיר־ גְּדוֹלָה֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים מַהֲלַ֖ךְ שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִֽים׃

passages.text: On the first day of his journey, Jonah set out into the city and proclaimed, “Forty more days and Nineveh will be overturned!”
passages.sermon:
Jonah was a prophet of the LORD.
God sent Jonah to Nineveh, a very large city.
Jonah entered Nineveh.
He began his journey into the city on the first day.
Jonah called out to the people.
He said, “In forty days, Nineveh will be overturned.”
passages.original: וַיָּ֤חֶל יוֹנָה֙ לָב֣וֹא בָעִ֔יר מַהֲלַ֖ךְ י֣וֹם אֶחָ֑ד וַיִּקְרָא֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר ע֚וֹד אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְנִֽינְוֵ֖ה נֶהְפָּֽכֶת׃

passages.text: And the Ninevites believed God. They proclaimed a fast and dressed in sackcloth, from the greatest of them to the least.
passages.sermon:
The people of Nineveh heard Jonah’s message from God.
The people of Nineveh believed God.
They decided to fast.
They put on sackcloth to show their sorrow.
Everyone did this.
The greatest people did it.
The least people did it.
passages.original: וַֽיַּאֲמִ֛ינוּ אַנְשֵׁ֥י נִֽינְוֵ֖ה בֵּֽאלֹהִ֑ים וַיִּקְרְאוּ־ צוֹם֙ וַיִּלְבְּשׁ֣וּ שַׂקִּ֔ים מִגְּדוֹלָ֖ם וְעַד־ קְטַנָּֽם׃

passages.text: When word reached the king of Nineveh, he got up from his throne, took off his royal robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
passages.sermon:
The king of Nineveh heard the message.
He got up from his throne.
He took off his royal robe.
He put on sackcloth.
He sat in ashes.
passages.original: וַיִּגַּ֤ע הַדָּבָר֙ אֶל־ מֶ֣לֶך נִֽינְוֵ֔ה וַיָּ֙קָם֙ מִכִּסְא֔וֹ וַיַּעֲבֵ֥ר אַדַּרְתּ֖וֹ מֵֽעָלָ֑יו וַיְכַ֣ס שַׂ֔ק וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב עַל־ הָאֵֽפֶר׃

passages.text: Then he issued a proclamation in Nineveh: “By the decree of the king and his nobles: Let no man or beast, herd or flock, taste anything at all. They must not eat or drink.
passages.sermon:
The king of Nineveh spoke to the people.
He made a proclamation in the city.
The king and his nobles gave this order.
No person may eat anything.
No animal may eat anything.
No herd or flock may eat anything.
No one may drink water.
No animal may drink water.
passages.original: וַיַּזְעֵ֗ק וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ בְּנִֽינְוֵ֔ה מִטַּ֧עַם הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וּגְדֹלָ֖יו לֵאמֹ֑ר הָאָדָ֨ם וְהַבְּהֵמָ֜ה הַבָּקָ֣ר וְהַצֹּ֗אן אַֽל־ יִטְעֲמוּ֙ מְא֔וּמָה אַ֨ל־ יִרְע֔וּ וּמַ֖יִם אַל־ יִשְׁתּֽוּ׃

passages.text: Furthermore, let both man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and have everyone call out earnestly to God. Let each one turn from his evil ways and from the violence in his hands.
passages.sermon:
The king of Nineveh spoke to the people and animals in the city.
He commanded that every person must wear sackcloth.
He commanded that every animal must wear sackcloth.
He told everyone to call out strongly to God.
He told each person to turn away from his evil ways.
He told each person to stop the violence he was doing.
passages.original: וְיִתְכַּסּ֣וּ שַׂקִּ֗ים הָֽאָדָם֙ וְהַבְּהֵמָ֔ה וְיִקְרְא֥וּ אֶל־ אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּחָזְקָ֑ה וְיָשֻׁ֗בוּ אִ֚ישׁ מִדַּרְכּ֣וֹ הָֽרָעָ֔ה וּמִן־ הֶחָמָ֖ס אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּכַפֵּיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Who knows? God may turn and relent; He may turn from His fierce anger, so that we will not perish.”
passages.sermon:
The people of Nineveh spoke.
They said, “Who knows?”
God may turn from His anger.
God may show mercy.
God may stop His fierce anger.
Then we will not die.
passages.original: מִֽי־ יוֹדֵ֣עַ יָשׁ֔וּב וְנִחַ֖ם הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְשָׁ֛ב מֵחֲר֥וֹן אַפּ֖וֹ וְלֹ֥א נֹאבֵֽד׃

passages.text: When God saw their actions—that they had turned from their evil ways—He relented from the disaster He had threatened to bring upon them.
passages.sermon:
God saw what the people did.
God saw that the people turned away from their evil ways.
God decided not to bring the disaster He had threatened.
God did not do what He said He would do to them.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤רְא הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶֽת־ מַ֣עֲשֵׂיהֶ֔ם כִּי־ שָׁ֖בוּ מִדַּרְכָּ֣ם הָרָעָ֑ה וַיִּנָּ֣חֶם הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים עַל־ הָרָעָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּ֥ר לַעֲשׂוֹת־ לָהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א עָשָֽׂה׃
